# Configuration reference

Every setting is environment-driven — nothing is stored in the repo.
Secrets come only from env or the host's secret store; **never commit
`.env`** (it's in `.gitignore` already).

Copy `.env.example` → `.env` and fill in, or run `scripts/setup.sh`
which writes a minimal `.env` for you. `python -m pa doctor` reports
what's configured and what's missing; `python -m pa check-config`
prints the resolved non-secret config. This file lists every variable
the code reads — `.env.example` has the same list with fuller comments.

<!-- generated by scripts/gen_config_docs.py — edit .env.example, then re-run it -->

## core

| var | default | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `PA_ENV` | production | development \| test \| production |
| `PA_ENV_FILE` | *(unset)* | python -m pa auto-loads .env from the working dir; PA_ENV_FILE points it at a different file (vars already in the environment always win). |
| `PA_DATA_DIR` | /data | Where SQLite and backups live (mount a volume here in production) |
| `PA_BIND` | 127.0.0.1 | Bind. Development: loopback only. Production: see docs/SECURITY.md - non-loopback is allowed only in the documented Fly topology, inside a container with PA_CONTAINER_BIND=true (publish rules = the boundary; compose publishes to host loopback only), or keep loopback behind a TLS terminator like Caddy. |
| `PA_PORT` | 8080 |  |
| `PA_CONTAINER_BIND` | *(unset)* | only inside Docker/compose deployments |
| `PA_TIMEZONE` | Europe/London | Scheduler default timezone (IANA name; per-schedule override exists) |
| `FLY_APP_NAME` | *(unset)* | Set automatically by Fly.io machines — its presence proves the TLS topology for non-loopback binds (docs/DEPLOY.md). Don't set it by hand. |
| `PA_SYSTEMD_SCOPE` | *(unset)* | Which unit the watchdog + self-update canary restart, and at which systemd scope (defaults match the documented user unit): scope=user -&gt; systemctl --user restart &lt;unit&gt; scope=system -&gt; systemctl restart &lt;unit&gt; |
| `PA_SYSTEMD_UNIT` | *(unset)* |  |

## Inference provider (owner-supplied OpenAI-compatible endpoint)

| var | default | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `LLM_BASE_URL` **required** | *(unset)* | Any OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint you control or pay for. https to any host, or http to loopback/private hosts only. LLM_API_KEY is optional ONLY for genuinely anonymous endpoints. Example: Groq -&gt; LLM_BASE_URL=https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 Example: local -&gt; LLM_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 (no key needed) |
| `LLM_MODEL` **required** | *(unset)* |  |
| `LLM_API_KEY` **required** | *(unset)* |  |
| `LLM_STREAMING` | false | SSE streaming on/off |
| `LLM_TOOLS` | true | set false for endpoints without tool calling |
| `LLM_COMPLETIONS_PATH` | *(unset)* | nonstandard endpoints only |

## Connections library (/connect <app> in Discord)

| var | default | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| `PA_SECRETS_KEY` | *(unset)* | Full guide: docs/CONNECTIONS.md. Owner runs /connect notion\|linear\|google\| url:https://... in Discord, signs in at the link, tools show up in chat. Encrypts every token blob at rest (AES-256-GCM). REQUIRED for /connect. Generate once with: python3 -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))" Never committed, never logged; losing it means reconnecting every app. |
| `PA_PUBLIC_URL` | *(unset)* | Public https base that OAuth providers redirect to — expose the web server with a free Cloudflare Tunnel (exact commands in docs/CONNECTIONS.md) and set the tunnel URL here. The callback is &lt;PA_PUBLIC_URL&gt;/oauth/callback — add exactly that as the redirect URI on OAuth apps you register yourself. |
| `PA_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | *(unset)* | Google OAuth client for `/connect google` (Gmail+Calendar). Falls back to the GMAIL_CLIENT_* pair above when unset — same client. |
| `PA_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | *(unset)* |  |
| `PA_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` | *(unset)* | GitHub's auth server has no dynamic client registration — register an OAuth App by hand (redirect URI = the callback above) for /connect github. |
| `PA_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` | *(unset)* |  |
| `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` | *(unset)* | Optional: Composio managed-auth fallback for apps not in the catalog. Free Hobby platform tier ~= 20k managed-app calls/month; a local counter warns you in Discord at 80%. Override the assumed cap if pricing changes: |
| `PA_COMPOSIO_MONTHLY_LIMIT` | *(unset)* |  |
| `PA_MCP_TIMEOUT` | *(unset)* | per-request seconds for MCP/OAuth calls |
| `COMPOSIO_API_BASE` | *(unset)* | API base |
| `COMPOSIO_USER_ID` | *(unset)* | user-id namespace the toolkit keys are |
| `PA_OWNER_EMAIL` | *(unset)* | stored under Multiple accounts per app: `/connect gmail` is the owner's (default) account; `/connect gmail account:pal` connects a second, labelled one — its tools are addressed 'gmail@pal.&lt;tool&gt;'. The owner's own email address — where pal's mailbox sends digests. REQUIRED for the email_owner chat tool (the only send that needs no approval — the recipient can only ever be this address). |

| `PA_HEALTH_RSS_MB` | *(unset)* | RSS ceiling for ok=true |
| `PA_HEALTH_EXPECT_WORKER` | *(unset)* | also require a fresh worker beat |
| `PA_HEALTH_WORKER_MAX_SECONDS` | *(unset)* | beat staleness limit |
| `PA_HEALTH_DISCORD` | *(unset)* | also require a live in-process |
| `PA_CALL_STREAM_BRAIN` | *(unset)* | Call brain: streamed tiny model on the router 'call' tier (default order groq -&gt; gemini-api -&gt; openrouter-free -&gt; cloudflare, api backends only, 4s per attempt). PA_CALL_STREAM_BRAIN=off restores the full chat-agent turn; PA_CALL_LLM_SECONDS tunes the per-backend cap. |
| `PA_ROUTER_CALL_ORDER` | *(unset)* |  |
| `PA_ROUTER_CALL_MODELS` | *(unset)* |  |
| `PA_CALL_LLM_SECONDS` | *(unset)* |  |
| `PA_TTS_CHARS_DAY` | *(unset)* | Call TTS budgets: daily char caps per provider; a spent provider is skipped before the call locks a voice. PA_TTS_CHARS_DAY sets one global cap; PA_TTS_CHARS_&lt;PROVIDER&gt;_DAY overrides per provider. |
| `PA_TTS_CHARS_AZURE_DAY` | *(unset)* |  |
| `PA_TTS_CHARS_CLOUDFLARE_DAY` | *(unset)* |  |
| `PA_TTS_CHARS_GEMINI_DAY` | *(unset)* |  |
| `PA_BROWSER_OWNER_DOMAINS` | *(unset)* | Account-owner registry: browser domains whose signed-in account is pal's (unknown domains fail closed to owner). Connections get owner_kind via the /connect 'whose account?' button. |
| `PA_POLICY_ENGINE` | *(unset)* | Policy engine: ONE approval floor across every action path. Default on — writes/sends/deletes/spends/settings/publishes on the OWNER's accounts always need an explicit Discord approval; allow rules and unattended runs cannot cover them. 'off' restores the legacy per-tool gates (emergency only). PA_POLICY_VAULT_UNATTENDED keeps vault writes unattended-free. |
| `PA_POLICY_VAULT_UNATTENDED` | *(unset)* |  |
| `PA_BUDGET_<RESOURCE>_<SCOPE>` | *(unset)* | Budgets: daily ledger (day Europe/London) by scope (owner-chat \| call \| background \| job:&lt;n&gt; \| task:&lt;id&gt;) and resource. Defaults: background &lt;= 30% of each daily quota, calls reserve 20% of TTS/STT/Live. Override any cap: &lt;n&gt; e.g. PA_BUDGET_ESCALATIONS_BACKGROUND=8 |
| `PA_TOOL_TOPK` | *(unset)* | Lean tool catalogue: prune the ReAct tool list to a core set + top-k keyword matches per turn; tools_more lists the rest. |

| `PA_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS` | *(unset)* | stuck task requeues after the lease |

| `PA_SESSION_IDLE_SECONDS` | *(unset)* | web session idle TTL |
| `PA_SESSION_ABSOLUTE_SECONDS` | *(unset)* | web session hard TTL |
| `PA_LOGIN_WINDOW_SECONDS` | *(unset)* | login-throttle window |
| `PA_LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES` | *(unset)* | failures in the window -&gt; lock |

| `PA_FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | *(unset)* | fetch tool per-request timeout |
| `PA_FETCH_MAX_REDIRECTS` | *(unset)* | fetch tool redirect limit |
